title: Canonical coefficient comparison is natural for transported kernel maps
statement: Let $j:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion, $L$ invertible, and $J=j.\ker$ satisfy $J^2=0$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sc-invertible-module, def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf, def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. For $n,a,b\geq0$ put $F=j^*(J\otimes L^n)$, $N=(j^*L)^n$, $K_r=\ker(\eta_{L^{n(r+1)}})$ [def-pc-module-pullback, lem-sc-square-zero-tensor-graded-presentation]. Form $t_r:K_r\simeq j_*(F\otimes N^r)$ by the inverse ideal-kernel comparison, the annihilated-module unit, and the coefficient-degree comparison [lem-sc-square-zero-ideal-tensor-unit]. For any module morphism $v:F\otimes N^a\to F\otimes N^b$, define $m=t_a;j_*v;t_b^{-1}$. The canonical coefficient cohomology comparisons $k_r$ [lem-sc-square-zero-ideal-tensor-unit] satisfy $H^1(X,m);k_b^{-1}=k_a^{-1};H^1(Z,v)$ as additive-group morphisms [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 09MS, coherent-equation-ses and its coefficient identifications; Tag 01XC, affine comparison; Tag 01F8, functoriality of cohomology.

proof.text: Construct t_r as the inverse canonical ideal-kernel comparison, the invertible square-zero ideal tensor unit, and pushforward of the coefficient-degree isomorphism. Define m by conjugation. All data are actual composites.

Use source and target naturality of moduleCohomologyFMap to obtain edge naturality for every module map. Expand the inverse canonical comparison into H(t_r) followed by the edge map. Apply edge naturality to the tensor-degree comparison; functoriality identifies the two composites.

The equation m;t_b=t_a;j_*v follows by inverse cancellation. Apply H, compose with the edge map, use edge naturality for v, and substitute the two inverse-comparison formulas. This gives the asserted commuting square.

proof_origin.place: Expanded naturality of the canonical coefficient comparison from Tag 09MS, using the affine edge comparison of Tag 01XC and functoriality of Tag 01F8.
